mbm-0926.clue: I have an assistant with a very long neck.
mbm-0926.quote: I make a silk scarf appear from a clay giraffe at our library show. A little girl fed it a paper leaf afterward. I’ve kept the leaf tucked inside for its next performance.

mbm-0927.clue: I count the waltz on my shirt buttons.
mbm-0927.quote: I embroidered a tiny dot on every third button of my dance shirt. My partner tapped one when I missed the turn. Now the tap means we’re doing beautifully.

mbm-0928.clue: I crocheted a hat with an exit.
mbm-0928.quote: My nephew wanted his curly ponytail outside the hat I made for him. I left a hole in the top. On windy days he looks like an especially pleased palm tree.

mbm-0929.quote: My father rented a lane for just the two of us after my first away game. We bowled slowly so our hour would last. I kept the orange wristband in my shoe bag.

mbm-0930.clue: I quilt with a toy train beside me.
mbm-0930.quote: I stitched an oval track onto my nephew’s blanket and made a little tunnel with a scrap of corduroy. His train disappears inside it every night and comes out for breakfast.

mbm-0931.clue: I bought one beautiful cup with two handles.
mbm-0931.quote: I found it on a market stall beside dozens of ordinary ones. My dad takes one handle and I take the other when we toast the first cherries of the summer.

mbm-0932.clue: Mum has two yellow coats on rainy mornings.
mbm-0932.quote: I used my last exposure on the puddle under our clothesline. Mum’s yellow coat hung upside down beside the moon in the water. She put the print above her coat hook. I've reached for the wrong sleeve twice.

mbm-0933.clue: I keep a feather next to the kettlebell.
mbm-0933.quote: My sister balanced a feather on my wrist to show me how much I was wobbling. I can lift the bell smoothly now. The feather still lives in the zipper of my gym bag.

mbm-0934.clue: I gave the queen a tiny bonnet.
mbm-0934.quote: The park chess set lost the top of its white queen. I crocheted a yellow cap to tell her apart. People ask to play our board because the queen looks ready for Sunday lunch.

mbm-0935.clue: I put a secret garden on the inside.
mbm-0935.quote: I tooled a little fern into the inside flap of my leather satchel. Most people only see the plain brown bag. The fern greets me whenever I go looking for a pencil.

mbm-0936.clue: I can play our cousin’s knock on the bellows.
mbm-0936.quote: My accordion lesson kept getting interrupted by family at the door. I turned their knock into the first three notes of a vallenato. Nobody knows whether to dance or answer it now.

mbm-0937.clue: I’ve got a disc that smells like basil.
mbm-0937.quote: My flying disc landed gently across the herb pots on our balcony. I carried the whole tray downstairs to show my throwing partner. We played another round and made pesto for lunch.

mbm-0938.clue: I keep the smallest hotel in a tin.
mbm-0938.quote: Our board game lost its last red hotel. My dad carved one from a matchstick and painted it with nail polish. We lift it with tweezers and charge a fortune for the view.

mbm-0939.clue: I’m learning the sky one tail at a time.
mbm-0939.quote: I drew the tail fins of every plane at the little air show. At home I cut them into cards for my niece. She can already match the red one to the right engine sound.

mbm-0940.clue: I saved the blue accordion strap.
mbm-0940.quote: My aunt’s old accordion needed a new shoulder strap. We stitched one from a blue dancing sash and played her wedding vallenato while the last thread was still hanging loose.

mbm-0941.clue: I can vanish a very patient lemon.
mbm-0941.quote: For my kitchen magic act I lift a bowl and the lemon vanishes. My nephew always opens the cupboard to make sure it’s comfortable. I leave a tiny paper pillow beside it for him.

mbm-0942.clue: I carry a tune in my lunchbox.
mbm-0942.quote: On market mornings I practice vallenato with my cousin before the stalls open. We keep the little metal scraper in my lunchbox. It shares the ride home with whatever mangoes are left.

mbm-0943.clue: I learned to tie a bow with an audience.
mbm-0943.quote: I pull a long ribbon from my empty hat and have a volunteer tie the last knot. My little brother made a bow so beautiful nobody wanted me to untie it. I bought a second hat.

mbm-0944.quote: At anime club we each pick a side character to sketch. I drew the gloomy tax collector and gave him a pet tortoise. He’s got his own fan club at our table now.

mbm-0945.clue: I make the moon disappear between courses.
mbm-0945.quote: I cut a silver paper moon for a dinner-table trick. When I tucked it into my sleeve the cat saw it go. She attends every show now, with her nose pointed at my cuff.

mbm-0946.clue: I gave my niece one end of the rope.
mbm-0946.quote: The knot is supposed to vanish when I shake the rope. My niece held tight and the knot stayed right there. She bowed first, so I introduced her as the world’s finest knot keeper.

mbm-0947.clue: I made a deck box that thinks it’s a castle.
mbm-0947.quote: I painted a drawbridge on the lid and tied it with green ribbon. When the ribbon comes loose the cards spill onto the table like little knights rushing to lunch.

mbm-0948.clue: I still dance with a milk ticket.
mbm-0948.quote: The club stamped my wrist with a tiny blue star the night my friend got her first DJ set. I pressed the stamp onto a milk ticket before it faded. It lives inside my record sleeve.

mbm-0949.clue: I can see the bass line through a glass.
mbm-0949.quote: At our local club the ice cubes in my ginger ale hopped against the sides when the DJ dropped the bass. I carried the glass back to my friend like a little dancing instrument.

mbm-0950.quote: My dad and I read the same mystery in different towns. We cut twin bookmarks from a cereal box and stop at the same chapter on Sundays, so neither of us gives away the good bits.
